result_text:
Template literals are now masked like the other string literals when units are compared, so the two JavaScript functions in your example should be reported as one duplicated unit. I checked this at the normalization level only; I did not run a full analysis over a JavaScript project to see the report entry.

**Change**

- `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`, `extraCleanContent`: added `replaceAll("(?s)`.*?`", "``")` before the double- and single-quote rules. Each backtick literal, including `${...}` interpolation and multi-line literals, collapses to ``` `` ```. It runs before the quote rules so a `"` or `'` inside a template can't pair with text outside it. The `/.+?/` rule now never sees template content either.
- `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest.java`: added `cleanContentTemplateLiterals`. It covers the `Hello alpha`/`Hello beta` case, a multi-line literal, and a code difference outside the literal that must still keep the units apart.

**Tests**

`mvn -o -pl codeanalyzer test` on the units and duplication test classes: all pass (CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest 10, JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest 2, UnitsExtractorTest 1, UnitUtilsTest 11, DuplicationAnalyzerTest 2, DuplicationEngineTest 1). Nothing was committed.
